page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core testing placing the instance in the top 10% of its class. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong single-core capabilities and excels in cryptographic operations, scoring in the top 10% for PassMark CPU encryption and extended instructions. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is exceptionally high at 8120.31 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds align with the historical average. Single-threaded gzip compression represents a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25%, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression recovers to a strong top-25% standing.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high compute density with a lower RAM-to-vCPU ratio, making it a cost-efficient choice for parallel processing tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads such as large-scale compilation, cryptography, parallel data decompression, and high-throughput Redis caching. It can also support moderate database operations and web serving, though memory-bound applications may find the 2.67 GB per core allocation restrictive.
